source.author: rcxdude
source.text: I see a bit of a split in people in creative roles of all kinds (and this is something I had noted before LLMs made the contrast more stark). some people get into it because they like the process of making the thing that they are making (in whole or in part). Others get into it because they have a thing that they want to exist in the world but no-one else has made it (I would also split this into people who just want the thing, or people who want to make something that crosses many domains and so want custom things that will fit into the whole). The former group tend to react with revulsion to automation, because it removes the part they like (though it may depend on what part is automated: most people will find some part of their work necessary but tedious). The latter are usually much more willing to embrace it, because it's the end result that they care about moreso than the process.
